newsitem.title: QATAR: Elf lifts output at Qatar oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Elf lifts output at Qatar oilfield.

text.p: A second well was commissioned on Thursday at the al-Khaleej oilfield offshore Qatar, boosting output to 10,000 barrels per day (bpd), field operators Elf Petroleum Qatar, a subsidiary of Elf Aquitaine, said.
"We put the second well on stream this morning... production has gone up to 10,000 bpd," Elf Petroleum Qatar's managing director Jean Philippe Magnon told Reuters.
Elf Petroleum Qatar has a 25-year production-sharing contract with state Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC) to develop al-Khaleej where it is operator with a 55 percent stake.
Agip Spa holds the remaining 45 percent.
Elf began operations at the field in March and aims to produce 30,000 bpd from al-Khaleej by year-end.
"We plan to drill a total of six wells to achieve and average output of 30,000 bpd by the year-end," said Magnon.
Crude from the field is sent by pipeline to Halul island where it is blended as part of Qatar Marine crude export grade.
